I'm probably not the target audience but for those looking to buy, it's a bullet hell with a few unique features/gimmicks. You pilot a boat that not only has tank controls but feels a little janky and each boat has different stats. To spawn enemies in you have to play a little 'mini-game' that looks similar to other fishing games that involve clicking at the right time to get a fish. There's also a couple of regions which have different fish. Each fish having a different pattern and time they spawn. Certainly a unique take on the bullet hell genre but I would say it feels boring, again maybe because I'm not the target audience. If what I said so far seems interesting though, maybe you'll have better luck enjoying the game.

Interesting idea with a flawed execution. Instead of being attacked by waves of enemies like most vampire survivors, in this one you choose to summon enemies, and they can be of 4 different difficulty tiers. Every time you kill an enemy, you heal 1 hp, so you want to spam weak enemies while fighting strong enemies. The problem is that every fight feels the same, you are focusing all of your attention of the QTE of summoning more enemies and it doesn't actually matter if you are sitting in a pack of enemies or not because you can heal faster than you take damage. On-top of this, there is an overarching mechanic to win the game that can only be unlocked by spending permanent currency, but it's grindy to get this currency. For reference you can summon 50 rare fish per day, and you'll probably only be capable of purchasing these fish on days 4-7. Each rare fish gives 10 bounty points, so about 200 rare fish or 2000 bounty for a full run focused on getting bounty. The unlock to be able to win the game is 250k (99k of which you can get from quests). Way too much

Like Vampire Survivors, but maybe with some fishing instead? FFM is the game that makes you feel like you are going to get that. I'm just going to lay it out, the controls make it alot less enjoyable, with positioning being painful. It's tank controls, but they wanted to make it part of the meta by making ramming or drifting a playstyle. Meaning that there are alot of upgrades to make you go very fast and accurate, but it requires so much investment in a RNG game that it leads to one conclusion; Half of the builds don't seem viable, so half of the upgrades are poison pills unless you hard commit and hope that you are lucky ontop of being lucky. It just makes the game tedious, and with a roguelike system that has alot of plateaus, power wise, your going to get bored. I like alot of things in the game, just not how they where implemented, but at the 4 hour mark, they haven't given me a reason to play further. Research is a grind, finding specific fish basically means your going to look it up, unlocks usually are gated. Research points are too few awarded for what they unlock, meaning the game feels the same for large parts, and the meta I am at means I have to do the following if I want to progress with any sense of speed: basically once you can catch sardines, you need to restart until them as the bounty, and gain several hundred research points per first level run, then repeat. The other methods are either incredibly inefficient, or too RNG based that trying to do the rare fish bounty and hoping you get an efficient build to actually kill when you do rare bait, makes the game feel like a waste of time. I love the vibe of the game, I can appreciate trying something different with the combat, but I can't get behind the terrible pacing, and I can't recommend that you should try it.

Classic "thumbs sideways". Clearly made with a lot of stuff in mind in general, but it does not come together for a fun enough gameplay loop. Mainly, as you will read in other reviews, handling of the boats is fairly atrocious and gets worse with ships with specifically low values in that attribute (yepp, its an actual variable). This matters a lot, because the way to kill fish for the first few hours from what I can tell either involves manual (!) - sigh - aim (harpoon) or being close enough (paddles) or, in some magic way, knowing where fish will be 2-20 seconds in advance (nets - horribly, horribly implemented). Overall its quite honestly VERY far away from the "Doomguy vs huge amounts of fish" that it kinda advertises itself at. Or at the very least, it keeps you at arms length of that for far too long to be advertising it. Thats sadly a classic dilemma..feels like they don't want to give you too much scaling too quickly, but the initial "needs skill to compensate being weak" ramp up phase is just absolutely ruined by the boats being slow, horrendous to handle and just not fun to play. Add to this that shooting fish is not impactful and that overall graphics are very rudimentary and it is hard to give this a thumbs up, no matter how much content there seems to be medium term. Sorry. Maybe if you figure out a way to not ruin the "I'm a zippy fisherman, but not super capable right away" compromise between crappy handling vs not being able to do direct control (steering is basically all momentum, like in old top down spaceship stuff, think Delta V Rings of Saturn - or SPAZ - acceleration / deceleration and drift and momentum) this could go somewhere. SPAZ did this fairly well (but that is because of missiles, auto-aim lasers etc), here its just annoying and timewastey.

Unfortunately I can't recommend Fish Fear Me. I absolutely loved Snake Farm and hoped for a similar experience. What made Snake Farm great was that it was tough, but fair. Fish Fear Me is tough, and unfair. First off, the boat is tough to control. Having done a bit of real world sailing, this is entirely accurate. However, for a game where accuracy and avoidance against fast moving enemies is of paramount importance, It is absolutely soul destroying. Second. The fish you catch are not auto collected. Which is a super added pain on a boat that is tough to control when you have to go back and collect. Especially when you choose a boat for speed, which is absolutely needed to outrun a lot of the fish, but has an insane and slow turning circle. And if you've chummed up more fish than you can handle, you aren't going back, you're just running. And almost any amount of fish is more fish than you can handle... Because 3. Each type of chum will bring up more than one type of fish. All of which need one of the different weapons to be most effective against. Which means that whatever weapon you start with, it will not be effective against at least one set of early fish. And you can't upgrade any weapon without obtaining money which comes from getting fish, which you can't get because you can't upgrade your weapons fast enough. The game even admits this by offering an upgrade of free money through overhealing and autohealing, which turns out to be one of the best strategies by far for money in the early game. 4. The two weapons you can start with which do autocollect, the krill and the net, both curse you to terrible boats and require lots of money just to get up to slightly effective against the second rank of fish. By the time you get there you've basically wasted all your allotted days in the game which is just enough days to feel like you're getting to parity with the basic fish and absolutely nowhere near enough days to feel like you're getting powerful enough to actually start dealing with the game. i.e. Just as soon as your build gets somewhere near actually working, your run is artificially ended. And it just goes on and on. In Snake Farm, all the aspects of the game worked with each other. You could choose to level up the enemies when you felt tough enough to take them on. You made your own balance and you paid the price if you over did things. Here everything works against each other. You can see that it's trying to work the same way but you are off balance from the start and you are just fighting the controls and the unfairness until it inevitably sinks you. Even if you only choose easy enemies at the start, you will have fish that are going to break your run, no matter what your starting loadout is. Nothing synergises. Nothing feels like a hard, but viable route. Instead it just feels like banging your head against a brick wall, only eventually, less fun. There are obvious events and triggers in the game, but absolutely no indication how to get anything started. The throne room in world 2 clearly shows what needs to be done. But not in any way how to do it. I could have consulted a guide, but I just stopped caring. It was pretty much guaranteed that any event was just going to kill me even faster. There is metaprogression, but it doesn't actually improve your chances in the game at all, at least not for the four hours of grinding I put into it to unlock a few other things that would have taken hours to get that also would not have improved my chances. It took me twice as long as the review period to realise that this was absolutely not going anywhere enjoyable. So I gave it a full fair chance. I would have refunded it if I could.
